subtitle: Lesson 60 · Migration, Translation & Capstone

code:
WITH SalesByTerritory AS (
  SELECT st.Name AS TerritoryName, soh.SalesPersonID,
         SUM(sod.LineTotal) AS TerritoryTotal
  FROM Sales.SalesOrderHeader soh
  JOIN Sales.SalesOrderDetail sod ON sod.SalesOrderID = soh.SalesOrderID
  JOIN Sales.SalesTerritory st ON st.TerritoryID = soh.TerritoryID
  GROUP BY st.Name, soh.SalesPersonID
)
SELECT p.FirstName + ' ' + p.LastName AS SalesPersonName,
       s.TerritoryName, s.TerritoryTotal,
       RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY s.TerritoryName ORDER BY s.TerritoryTotal DESC)
FROM SalesByTerritory s
JOIN Person.Person p ON p.BusinessEntityID = s.SalesPersonID;
caption: A JOIN, a GROUP BY aggregate, a CTE + window function, and string concatenation -- all in one.

code:
-- T-SQL:       FirstName + ' ' + LastName
-- Oracle:      first_name || ' ' || last_name
-- PostgreSQL:  first_name || ' ' || last_name
-- MySQL:       CONCAT(first_name, ' ', last_name)
--   (|| means logical OR on MySQL by default!)
caption: MySQL is the one real outlier -- CONCAT() is the only safe choice.

-- Oracle & PostgreSQL: identical syntax to T-SQL, no changes
-- MySQL: identical syntax too -- BUT only from MySQL 8.0 onward
--   Earlier MySQL needs derived subqueries + manual rank logic
caption: Always confirm the MySQL version before assuming this translates directly.
